description: %Pt{x: 1, y: 2} == %{__struct__: Pt, x: 1, y: 2} is true. TermComparator (runtime/src/term.rs) sorts a value into a Category of the term order; a named struct is in the map category, after every tuple. Maps compare by size, then keys, then values in key order through MapTerm, which reads either layout; two structs of one schema skip to their fields. There is no map hash: key lookup, uniq, MapSet, in and pins all go through the comparator. A value prints as %Name{...} exactly when its __struct__ names a struct whose schema the runtime holds and its keys are exactly that schema's fields (Heap::entries_spelling_a_struct); otherwise it prints as a map. Removed struct_cmp and SchemaIdentity::semantic_cmp. Fixture 00868 on all three paths. Not covered by the oracle: the key order of a printed map that names a module but is not its struct, where Elixir prints in VM atom order and fz in term order (the standing difference recorded in .agent/docs/any-value.md).
title: Equality, ordering and printing of a struct are layout-blind
